title: Oxidative phosphorylation and chemiosmosis; Anaerobic respiration; Link reaction and Krebs cycle; Cell signaling and receptors (general)
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: RS02#t2 term and clue written for the game; RS03b#t1 term and clue written for the game; RS02#t4 term and clue written for the game; RS03b#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: HO08a#N.3, RS04#N.3b, HO08a#N.5a, HO08a#N.8.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Matrix
items.clue: The fluid enclosed by the inner mitochondrial membrane.

items.label: Photophosphorylation
items.clue: Name for ATP production in a chloroplast driven by light.

items.label: Outer membrane
items.clue: Smooth boundary layer that encloses the whole mitochondrion.

items.label: ATP synthase
items.clue: Enzyme in the thylakoid membrane through which H⁺ flow back out.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between a ligand and its receptor?

options.text: The receptor's binding site converts the ligand into a product, in the way an enzyme's active site converts a substrate.
The ligand binds reversibly to a binding site on the receptor protein that is complementary to it, and the receptor changes shape.
Any ligand reaching a cell binds to it, because every cell carries receptors for every signalling chemical in the body.
The ligand passes through a channel in the receptor into the cytoplasm, where it brings about the response directly.

questions.explanation: Binding is reversible and does not alter the ligand; the receptor's change of shape starts the cell's response.

questions.stem: A mutant strain of a hypothetical yeast species cannot convert pyruvate into ethanol and CO₂. Wild-type and mutant cells are placed in a glucose solution with no O₂. Which prediction is best supported?

options.text: Glycolysis soon stops in the mutant but not the wild type, as NAD⁺ is not regenerated from NADH.
Glycolysis continues in the mutant, but it makes less ATP, as the fermentation step makes the ATP.
Glycolysis continues in the mutant, as NADH passes electrons through the ETC to CO₂ instead.
Glycolysis stops in both strains, as glycolysis needs O₂ to oxidize glucose to pyruvate.

questions.stem: At a synapse between a motor neuron and a muscle cell, the neuron releases the neurotransmitter acetylcholine, which causes the muscle cell to contract. Which statement correctly describes how this signal reaches the muscle cell?

options.text: It diffuses across the narrow gap between the neuron and the muscle cell next to it.
It is carried in the blood from the neuron to muscle cells all over the body.
It crosses the gap as an electric current that jumps from the neuron into the muscle cell.
It moves toward the muscle cell, because the muscle cell needs it in order to contract.

questions.stem: Vibrio fischeri produces light when packed at high density inside the light organ of a squid, but not when living at low density in seawater. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The squid releases a chemical into its light organ that switches on the light-producing genes of the bacteria living there.
Each bacterium switches on its light-producing genes independently when its supply of nutrients in the light organ is high enough.
Autoinducer secreted by each cell only reaches the threshold that switches on the light-producing genes when cells are dense.
The autoinducer accumulating in the light organ is itself the substance that gives out light when it reaches high concentration.
